title: Foundation F5
subtitle: Food, Health and Body
description: Twelve coordinated lessons that move from food and meals to preferences, restaurant transactions, body language, health problems, advice, sustained speaking and writing, and a complete four-skills assessment.

lessons.title: Food and Drinks
lessons.summary: Name a broad range of foods and drinks, classify them accurately, and use أُحِبُّ / لَا أُحِبُّ in meaningful sentences.
objectives: Recognise and pronounce common food and drink vocabulary.
Separate foods from drinks and notice noun gender where it supports agreement.
Express a like and a dislike using complete Arabic sentences.
Understand a short food-and-drink description.
success: I can name at least twelve foods and six drinks.
I can say what I like and do not like.
I can read fully vowelled food words accurately.
I can write three connected preference sentences.

patterns.en: I like bread and cheese.
patterns.tip: After أُحِبُّ, use the food as the object.

patterns.en: I do not like coffee.
patterns.tip: Put لَا directly before the present-tense verb.

patterns.en: I drink water and juice.
patterns.tip: Use أَشْرَبُ with drinks.

patterns.en: Do you like fish?
patterns.tip: Use هَلْ to make a yes/no question.

teach: Arabic food words become useful only when they are placed in a sentence. Learn the noun, then immediately combine it with أُحِبُّ، لَا أُحِبُّ، آكُلُ or أَشْرَبُ.
Some food words are collective nouns: تُفَّاحٌ can mean apples as a type of food, while تُفَّاحَةٌ means one apple. At this stage, prioritise accurate recognition and useful communication.

sorter.title: Food or drink?
sorter.instructions: Choose the correct category for each item.

listening.title: What does Huda like?
listening.script: اِسْمِي هُدَى. أُحِبُّ الخُبْزَ وَالجُبْنَ وَالتُّفَّاحَ. فِي الوَجْبَةِ الخَفِيفَةِ آكُلُ المُكَسَّرَاتِ أَوِ البِسْكُوِيتَ. لَا أُحِبُّ السَّمَكَ، وَلَا أَشْرَبُ القَهْوَةَ. أَشْرَبُ المَاءَ وَعَصِيرَ البُرْتُقَالِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

questions.prompt: Which two foods does Huda like together?
Which drinks does she have every day?
What does Huda have as a snack?
questions.feedback: She says آكُلُ المُكَسَّرَاتِ أَوِ البِسْكُوِيتَ.

reading.title: A family shopping note
reading.text: نَحْنُ نَشْتَرِي خُبْزًا وَأَرُزًّا وَدَجَاجًا لِلْعَشَاءِ. نَحْتَاجُ أَيْضًا إِلَى زَيْتٍ وَمِلْحٍ وَقَلِيلٍ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ. أُمِّي تُحِبُّ السَّلَطَةَ مَعَ الخَسِّ وَالطَّمَاطِمِ وَالبَصَلِ، وَأَبِي يُحِبُّ الحَسَاءَ. أَخِي لَا يُحِبُّ الخَضْرَوَاتِ، وَلٰكِنَّهُ يُحِبُّ الفَاكِهَةَ، خُصُوصًا المَوْزَ وَالعِنَبَ. نَشْتَرِي أَحْيَانًا الرُّوبِيَانَ وَمَأْكُولَاتٍ بَحْرِيَّةً، وَنَشْتَرِي أَيْضًا حَلِيبًا وَمَاءً.

questions.prompt: What is the family buying for dinner?
questions.feedback: The opening sentence lists خُبْزًا وَأَرُزًّا وَدَجَاجًا.

questions.prompt: Which fruit does he especially like?
questions.feedback: The text says خُصُوصًا المَوْزَ وَالعِنَبَ.
The final sentence gives حَلِيبًا وَمَاءً.

questions.prompt: Which three ingredients are needed in addition to the main foods?
options: oil, salt and a little sugar
questions.feedback: The text lists زَيْتٍ وَمِلْحٍ وَقَلِيلٍ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ.

questions.prompt: What is included in the mother’s salad?
questions.feedback: The salad contains الخَسِّ وَالطَّمَاطِمِ وَالبَصَلِ.

prompts: مَا طَعَامُكَ المُفَضَّلُ؟ / مَا طَعَامُكِ المُفَضَّلُ؟
model: Yes, I like salad a lot.

writing.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about foods and drinks you like and dislike. Include at least four food words, two drinks, وَ and one negative sentence.
checklist: Use أُحِبُّ and لَا أُحِبُّ.
Include at least one sentence with آكُلُ or أَشْرَبُ.
Join ideas with وَ or وَلٰكِنْ.
Check the Arabic spelling against the lesson bank.
writing.model: أُحِبُّ الخُبْزَ وَالجُبْنَ، وَأُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ أَيْضًا. لَا أُحِبُّ السَّمَكَ، وَلٰكِنِّي أُحِبُّ الدَّجَاجَ. آكُلُ الأَرُزَّ كَثِيرًا، وَأَشْرَبُ المَاءَ وَالعَصِيرَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

mistakes.why: أُحِبُّ takes a direct object; do not add إِلَى.
The first-person form is أُحِبُّ.
آكُلُ begins with a long ā written آ.

differentiation.core: Name eight foods and four drinks with picture or English support.
differentiation.develop: Ask and answer four preference questions, then report one classmate’s answer.
differentiation.stretch: Add collective/singular contrasts such as تُفَّاحٌ / تُفَّاحَةٌ and produce an 8-sentence food profile.

final.feedback: لَا أُحِبُّ = I do not like.

final.prompt: Which sentence asks a yes/no question?

grammar.title: Using أُحِبُّ / لَا أُحِبُّ with food nouns
grammar.arabic: اِسْتِعْمَالُ أُحِبُّ وَلَا أُحِبُّ مَعَ أَسْمَاءِ الطَّعَامِ
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is the opinion frame أُحِبُّ / لَا أُحِبُّ. Build a complete sentence by placing the food or drink directly after the verb, then notice the gender of the noun so later adjectives can agree accurately.

rules.heading: Say what you like
rules.explanation: أُحِبُّ means “I like”. The food or drink follows directly; do not add a preposition between the verb and the noun.

rules.heading: Make the opinion negative
rules.explanation: Put لَا immediately before أُحِبُّ. The rest of the sentence stays in the same order.

rules.heading: Notice noun gender
rules.explanation: Many food words are masculine, but some are feminine. Learn the noun with its gender because later description words must agree.

rules.heading: Ask another person
rules.explanation: Use تُحِبُّ for a male listener and تُحِبِّينَ for a female listener.

grammar.common_error: Do not write أُحِبُّ إِلَى الخُبْزِ. أُحِبُّ takes the food or drink directly: أُحِبُّ الخُبْزَ.

quiz.feedback: أَشْرَبُ is the first-person verb for drinking.

quiz.prompt: Make the sentence negative: أُحِبُّ القَهْوَةَ.
quiz.feedback: Put لَا immediately before the present-tense verb.

quiz.prompt: Ask a boy “Do you like fish?”
quiz.feedback: تُحِبُّ addresses a male listener.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct action?
quiz.feedback: Milk is a drink, so use أَشْرَبُ.

quiz.prompt: Which verb normally begins with أَـ because the speaker is “I”?
quiz.feedback: آكُلُ means “I eat”.
Use تُحِبُّ when asking a male listener.
قَهْوَةٌ is feminine.
لَا comes immediately before the correct first-person form أُحِبُّ.

builders.target: I like bread and cheese.
I do not drink coffee.
Do you like fish?

lessons.title: Meals and Eating Routines
lessons.summary: Describe breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks with time expressions, present-tense eating verbs and connected meal sentences.
objectives: Name meals and common meal-time expressions.
Use آكُلُ، أَشْرَبُ and أَتَنَاوَلُ accurately.
Say what you eat and drink at different times of day.
Read and understand a short daily meal routine.
success: I can name breakfast, lunch, dinner and a snack.
I can describe all three main meals.
I can ask مَاذَا تَأْكُلُ فِي ...؟
I can write a connected meal routine.

patterns.en: I eat bread and eggs for breakfast.
patterns.tip: Use فِي + the meal.

patterns.en: I have lunch at midday.
patterns.tip: أَتَنَاوَلُ can introduce the whole meal.

patterns.en: I drink milk in the morning.
patterns.tip: Time phrases can come at the end or beginning.

patterns.en: What do you eat for dinner? (to a female)
patterns.tip: Use تَأْكُلِينَ when addressing a female.

teach: A meal description needs more than a food list. Add the meal, a verb and a time phrase so that the listener knows when the action happens.
The verb أَتَنَاوَلُ is useful in formal Modern Standard Arabic for “I have/eat a meal”. Keep آكُلُ and أَشْرَبُ secure first, then use أَتَنَاوَلُ to vary language.

sorter.title: Match the routine to the time
sorter.instructions: Place each phrase under the most suitable time.

items.label: أَتَنَاوَلُ وَجْبَةً مَعَ عَائِلَتِي بَعْدَ العَمَلِ

listening.title: Rami’s meal routine
listening.script: فِي الصَّبَاحِ أَتَنَاوَلُ الفُطُورَ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ. آكُلُ الخُبْزَ وَالجُبْنَ، وَأَشْرَبُ الحَلِيبَ. عِنْدَ الظُّهْرِ آكُلُ الأَرُزَّ وَالدَّجَاجَ فِي المَدْرَسَةِ. بَعْدَ المَدْرَسَةِ آكُلُ تُفَّاحَةً. فِي المَسَاءِ أَتَنَاوَلُ العَشَاءَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي، وَأَشْرَبُ المَاءَ.

questions.prompt: What does he drink at breakfast?

reading.title: My three meals
reading.text: اِسْمِي سَارَةُ. عَادَةً أَتَنَاوَلُ فُطُورًا صِحِّيًّا: آكُلُ الزَّبَادِي وَالفَاكِهَةَ، وَأَشْرَبُ المَاءَ. فِي الغَدَاءِ آكُلُ السَّلَطَةَ وَالسَّمَكَ، وَلٰكِنِّي أَحْيَانًا آكُلُ البِيتْزَا مَعَ صَدِيقَاتِي. فِي العَشَاءِ تَطْبُخُ أُمِّي الحَسَاءَ أَوِ الأَرُزَّ وَالدَّجَاجَ. نَأْكُلُ مَعًا فِي المَسَاءِ.

questions.prompt: How does Sara describe her breakfast?
What does she eat with fruit?
Which lunch does she sometimes eat with friends?
What does the family do together?
questions.feedback: They eat together in the evening.

model: What do you eat for breakfast?
I eat bread and eggs and drink tea.
And when do you have lunch?
I have lunch at one o’clock.

writing.prompt: Write 6–8 sentences describing your meals on a normal day. Include breakfast, lunch, dinner, one snack, two time expressions and one frequency word.
checklist: Use a different verb at least twice: آكُلُ / أَشْرَبُ / أَتَنَاوَلُ.
Name all three main meals.
Use عَادَةً، أَحْيَانًا or دَائِمًا.
Join the routine with وَ، ثُمَّ or وَلٰكِنْ.
writing.model: عَادَةً أَتَنَاوَلُ الفُطُورَ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ. آكُلُ الخُبْزَ وَالجُبْنَ، وَأَشْرَبُ الحَلِيبَ. عِنْدَ الظُّهْرِ آكُلُ الغَدَاءَ فِي المَدْرَسَةِ. بَعْدَ المَدْرَسَةِ أَحْيَانًا آكُلُ وَجْبَةً خَفِيفَةً. فِي المَسَاءِ أَتَنَاوَلُ العَشَاءَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي، ثُمَّ أَشْرَبُ المَاءَ.

mistakes.why: Use أَشْرَبُ with a drink.
أَتَنَاوَلُ needs the meal/object; فِي الغَدَاءِ introduces what is eaten at lunch.
After فِي, the noun is in the genitive form: العَشَاءِ.

differentiation.core: Complete three sentence frames for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
differentiation.develop: Describe a full day with time and frequency language, then ask a partner two questions.
differentiation.stretch: Compare weekday and weekend meals and explain one difference in 8–10 sentences.

final.prompt: Choose the correct question to a female.

final.feedback: وَجْبَةٌ خَفِيفَةٌ means a light meal/snack.

grammar.title: آكُلُ / أَشْرَبُ with meals and فِي
grammar.arabic: آكُلُ وَأَشْرَبُ مَعَ الوَجَبَاتِ وَحَرْفِ الجَرِّ فِي
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is choosing the correct action—آكُلُ for food and أَشْرَبُ for drink—then locating the action at a meal with فِي.

rules.heading: Choose the correct action
rules.explanation: Use آكُلُ with solid food and أَشْرَبُ with drinks.

rules.heading: Add the meal
rules.formula: فِي الفُطُورِ / فِي الغَدَاءِ / فِي العَشَاءِ
rules.explanation: Use فِي before the meal when you mean “at/for breakfast, lunch or dinner”.

rules.heading: Ask what someone eats
rules.explanation: The verb ending changes for a female listener.

rules.heading: Use أَتَنَاوَلُ for a whole meal
rules.explanation: أَتَنَاوَلُ means “I have/eat” a meal and is useful in more formal descriptions.

grammar.common_error: Do not use آكُلُ with a drink. Say أَشْرَبُ الحَلِيبَ, not آكُلُ الحَلِيبَ.

quiz.feedback: The feminine third-person form begins with تَـ.
فِي الصَّبَاحِ is a time phrase.

quiz.prompt: Ask a girl what she eats for dinner.
quiz.feedback: Use تَأْكُلِينَ for a female listener.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence is a complete routine?
quiz.feedback: It gives an action, food and meal.

quiz.prompt: Which verb is most formal for “I have a meal”?
quiz.feedback: أَتَنَاوَلُ introduces having/eating a meal.
يَتَنَاوَلُ means “he has/eats”.
After فِي, use the genitive meal form الغَدَاءِ.

quiz.prompt: Choose “What do you drink at breakfast?” to a girl.
quiz.feedback: The female listener form ends in ـِينَ.

builders.target: In the morning I have breakfast at seven.
She eats rice and chicken for lunch.
What do you eat for dinner? (to a girl)

lessons.title: Likes, Dislikes and Preferences
lessons.summary: Extend food opinions with أُفَضِّلُ, comparisons, intensity words and accurate questions for different addressees.
objectives: Use أُحِبُّ، لَا أُحِبُّ and أُفَضِّلُ in food contexts.
Compare two foods using أَكْثَرَ مِنْ.
Ask male and female classmates about preferences.
Understand stated and implied preferences in short texts.
success: I can give at least three different food opinions.
I can compare two foods.
I can ask a male or female about a preference.
I can explain a classmate’s preference in the third person.

items.en: which of the two do you prefer? (m)
which of the two do you prefer? (f)

patterns.en: I prefer fish more than meat.
patterns.tip: Use أَكْثَرَ مِنْ before the second item.

patterns.en: I like dates a lot.
patterns.tip: Intensity words usually follow the opinion/object.

patterns.en: Which do you prefer: tea or coffee? (to a female)
patterns.tip: أَمْ links alternatives in a question.

patterns.ar: هِيَ تُفَضِّلُ العَصِيرَ، وَلَا تُحِبُّ الحَلِيبَ.
patterns.en: She prefers juice and does not like milk.
patterns.tip: Report another person using يـ / تـ verb forms.

teach: Preferences are personal, so there is no “correct” favourite food. The accuracy comes from the language used to express and compare the preference.
Do not confuse أُفَضِّلُ “I prefer” with أَفْضَلُ “better/best”. In this lesson, use the verb with an object: أُفَضِّلُ العَصِيرَ.

sorter.title: Like, dislike or prefer?
sorter.instructions: Sort each sentence by the type of opinion it expresses.

listening.title: Four food choices
listening.script: يُفَضِّلُ سَامِرٌ التَّمْرَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ الكَعْكِ. أَمَّا لَيْلَى فَتُحِبُّ الحَسَاءَ وَلَا تُحِبُّ البِيتْزَا. يُحِبُّ عُمَرُ العَصِيرَ، وَلٰكِنَّهُ يُفَضِّلُ المَاءَ لِأَنَّهُ يَشْرَبُهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. تُفَضِّلُ نُورٌ السَّمَكَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ.

questions.prompt: What does Samir prefer to cake?

questions.feedback: He likes juice but prefers water.

questions.prompt: What does Nour prefer to meat?

reading.title: A class food survey
reading.text: سَأَلْنَا عَشَرَةَ طُلَّابٍ عَنْ طَعَامِهِمُ المُفَضَّلِ. أَرْبَعَةُ طُلَّابٍ يُفَضِّلُونَ الدَّجَاجَ، وَثَلَاثَةٌ يُفَضِّلُونَ البِيتْزَا. طَالِبَانِ يُحِبَّانِ السَّمَكَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ، وَطَالِبَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ لَا تُحِبُّ اللَّحْمَ وَلَا السَّمَكَ؛ فَهِيَ تُفَضِّلُ الطَّعَامَ النَّبَاتِيَّ. أَمَّا المَشْرُوبُ المُفَضَّلُ فَهُوَ المَاءُ.

questions.prompt: What did two students prefer to meat?
Why does one student choose vegetarian food?
questions.feedback: The text explicitly says she likes neither meat nor fish.

model: Which do you prefer: tea or coffee?
I prefer tea more than coffee.
Yes, I like it a lot.

writing.prompt: Create a short report about your preferences and one other person’s preferences. Write 7–8 sentences and include one comparison.
checklist: Use أُحِبُّ، لَا أُحِبُّ and أُفَضِّلُ.
Include أَكْثَرَ مِنْ correctly.
Use هُوَ / هِيَ with the correct verb form.
Add one intensity word such as كَثِيرًا or جِدًّا.
writing.model: أُحِبُّ الفَاكِهَةَ كَثِيرًا، خُصُوصًا التُّفَّاحَ. لَا أُحِبُّ القَهْوَةَ. أُفَضِّلُ السَّمَكَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ. صَدِيقَتِي تُحِبُّ الدَّجَاجَ، وَلَا تُحِبُّ السَّلَطَةَ. هِيَ تُفَضِّلُ العَصِيرَ أَكْثَرَ مِنَ الحَلِيبِ.

mistakes.why: أُفَضِّلُ is the verb “I prefer”.
Use the complete comparison chunk أَكْثَرَ مِنْ.
With هِيَ, the present-tense verb begins with تـ.

differentiation.core: Choose and say three likes/dislikes using a displayed sentence frame.
differentiation.develop: Compare three food pairs and report a partner’s answers.
differentiation.stretch: Summarise class survey results using numbers and plural verb forms.

final.feedback: طَعَامِي المُفَضَّلُ means my favourite food.

grammar.title: أُفَضِّلُ and comparisons with أَكْثَرَ مِنْ
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus moves from a simple like to a comparison. Use أُفَضِّلُ for the preferred item and the complete chunk أَكْثَرَ مِنْ to compare it with another.

rules.heading: State a preference
rules.explanation: أُفَضِّلُ is a verb meaning “I prefer”. It is followed by the preferred item.

rules.heading: Compare two items
rules.explanation: Name the preferred item first, then use the complete comparison chunk أَكْثَرَ مِنْ.

rules.heading: Change the verb for the person
rules.explanation: Use يُـ with هُوَ and تُـ with هِيَ.

rules.heading: Ask between alternatives
rules.explanation: Use أَمْ between two named alternatives.

grammar.common_error: Do not confuse أُفَضِّلُ (“I prefer”) with أَفْضَلُ (“better/best”).

quiz.feedback: Use the verb أُفَضِّلُ for “I prefer”.
أَكْثَرَ مِنْ introduces the less-preferred comparison item.
أَمْ links the two alternatives.
The feminine third-person verb begins with تَـ.
كَثِيرًا means “a lot”.
The feminine listener form ends in ـِينَ.

quiz.prompt: Complete the comparison: أُفَضِّلُ الشَّايَ ___ القَهْوَةِ.
quiz.feedback: The full comparison chunk is أَكْثَرَ مِنْ.
With هِيَ, use تُفَضِّلُ.

builders.target: I prefer fish more than meat.
She likes soup but does not like pizza.
Which do you prefer: tea or coffee? (to a girl)

lessons.title: Giving Reasons: Taste and Health
lessons.summary: Justify food opinions using لِأَنَّهُ / لِأَنَّهَا and make taste and health adjectives agree with masculine and feminine nouns.
objectives: Use because-clauses to justify opinions.
Describe taste, temperature and health value with accurate adjective agreement.
Classify foods as healthy or less healthy without moralising personal choices.
Read a short balanced food review.
success: I can give a reason for a food opinion.
I can choose لِأَنَّهُ or لِأَنَّهَا.
I can use at least eight descriptive adjectives.
I can repair an agreement error.

patterns.en: I like soup because it is delicious and light.
patterns.tip: حَسَاءٌ is masculine → لِأَنَّهُ + masculine adjectives.

patterns.en: I prefer salad because it is healthy and fresh.
patterns.tip: سَلَطَةٌ is feminine → لِأَنَّهَا + feminine adjectives.

patterns.en: I do not like coffee because it is bitter.
patterns.tip: Agreement follows the noun, not the speaker.

patterns.ar: فِي رَأْيِي، الفَاكِهَةُ مُغَذِّيَةٌ، وَلٰكِنَّ الكَعْكَ حُلْوٌ جِدًّا.
patterns.en: In my opinion, fruit is nutritious, but cake is very sweet.
patterns.tip: Use contrast to make a balanced opinion.

teach: Arabic adjectives agree with the noun they describe. First identify whether the noun is masculine or feminine; then select both the correct pronoun in the reason and the matching adjective form.
“Healthy” and “unhealthy” describe nutritional patterns, not a person’s worth. Use language precisely and avoid turning food discussion into judgement.

sorter.title: Masculine or feminine reason?
sorter.instructions: Sort each noun phrase under the reason starter it requires.

listening.title: Which reason do you hear?
listening.script: أُحِبُّ السَّلَطَةَ لِأَنَّهَا طَازَجَةٌ وَصِحِّيَّةٌ. أُفَضِّلُ الحَسَاءَ لِأَنَّهُ دَافِئٌ وَخَفِيفٌ. لَا أُحِبُّ القَهْوَةَ لِأَنَّهَا مُرَّةٌ. أُحِبُّ التَّمْرَ لِأَنَّهُ حُلْوٌ وَمُغَذٍّ.

reading.title: A balanced café review
reading.text: زُرْتُ مَقْهًى صَغِيرًا مَعَ أُسْرَتِي. أَكَلْتُ حَسَاءَ العَدَسِ، وَأَحْبَبْتُهُ لِأَنَّهُ دَافِئٌ وَلَذِيذٌ. أَخَذَتْ أُخْتِي سَلَطَةً طَازَجَةً لِأَنَّهَا تُفَضِّلُ الطَّعَامَ الخَفِيفَ. كَانَ العَصِيرُ حُلْوًا جِدًّا، وَلٰكِنَّ المَاءَ كَانَ بَارِدًا وَمُنْعِشًا. فِي رَأْيِي، الوَجْبَةُ جَيِّدَةٌ وَمُتَوَازِنَةٌ.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer like lentil soup?
Why did the sister choose salad?
What criticism is made of the juice?
How is the whole meal described?

model: Because it is fresh and healthy.

writing.prompt: Write a short review of three foods or drinks. Give a clear opinion and at least one accurate reason for each.
checklist: Choose لِأَنَّهُ or لِأَنَّهَا from the noun gender.
Make every adjective agree.
Include one positive and one negative judgement.
Use فِي رَأْيِي and وَلٰكِنْ to connect ideas.
writing.model: فِي رَأْيِي، الحَسَاءُ لَذِيذٌ لِأَنَّهُ دَافِئٌ وَخَفِيفٌ. أُحِبُّ السَّلَطَةَ لِأَنَّهَا طَازَجَةٌ وَصِحِّيَّةٌ. لَا أُحِبُّ القَهْوَةَ لِأَنَّهَا مُرَّةٌ، وَلٰكِنِّي أُحِبُّ عَصِيرَ اللَّيْمُونِ لِأَنَّهُ مُنْعِشٌ.

mistakes.why: سَلَطَةٌ is feminine, so both the pronoun and adjective are feminine.
قَهْوَةٌ is feminine.
خُبْزٌ is masculine.

differentiation.core: Complete six reason sentences by choosing masculine or feminine forms.
differentiation.develop: Describe and justify opinions about four foods without a sentence frame.
differentiation.stretch: Write a balanced café review that evaluates taste, health and value using contrasting viewpoints.

final.feedback: Use لِأَنَّهَا for a feminine noun.
It contains an opinion and a reason.
The adjective agrees with feminine قَهْوَةٌ.

grammar.title: لِأَنَّهُ / لِأَنَّهَا and adjective agreement
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is a complete agreement chain: the reason pronoun and the adjective both agree with the food noun being described.

rules.heading: Give a reason for a masculine noun
rules.explanation: Use ـهُ when the food noun is masculine, then use a masculine adjective.

rules.heading: Give a reason for a feminine noun
rules.explanation: Use ـهَا when the food noun is feminine, then add the feminine adjective ending ـة.

rules.heading: Describe taste accurately
rules.explanation: The adjective changes to match the grammatical gender of the noun.

rules.heading: Join two reasons
rules.explanation: One reason sentence can contain two agreeing adjectives.

grammar.common_error: Agreement follows the noun, not the speaker: السَّلَطَةُ لِأَنَّهَا صِحِّيَّةٌ.

quiz.feedback: الحَسَاءُ is masculine.
The adjective agrees with feminine سَلَطَةٌ.
القَهْوَةُ is feminine singular.
وَلٰكِنْ means “but”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct reason for الخُبْزُ.
quiz.feedback: Masculine singular noun → ـهُ and masculine adjective.
The adjective agrees with its noun.
The feminine pronoun and adjective must agree.
Masculine noun → ـهُ → masculine adjective.

builders.target: I like soup because it is delicious and light.
I prefer salad because it is healthy.
Fruit is nutritious, but cake is very sweet.

lessons.title: Ordering Food Politely
lessons.summary: Complete a café or restaurant transaction: attract attention, request items, ask about availability and price, respond to questions and close politely.
objectives: Use polite request language in a food-ordering exchange.
Ask whether an item is available and request alternatives.
Understand common waiter/customer questions.
Write a complete six-line restaurant dialogue.
success: I can order at least three items politely.
I can ask هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ ...؟ and كَمِ السِّعْرُ؟
I can respond to a waiter’s clarification question.
I can close the transaction appropriately.

patterns.ar: أُرِيدُ حَسَاءَ العَدَسِ وَسَلَطَةً، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
patterns.en: I would like lentil soup and a salad, please.
patterns.tip: Use أُرِيدُ + item and finish with politeness.

patterns.en: Do you have vegetarian food?
patterns.tip: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ checks availability.

patterns.en: Still water, please.
patterns.tip: Short transactional replies can still be complete and polite.

patterns.en: The bill, please.
patterns.tip: Use a polite attention phrase to close the transaction.

patterns.ar: يَطْلُبُ الزَّبُونُ الحَسَاءَ، وَتَطْلُبُ الزَّبُونَةُ السَّلَطَةَ.
patterns.en: The male customer orders soup, and the female customer orders salad.
patterns.tip: The verb changes with the person being described.

teach: Transactional speaking rewards successful communication. Listen to the whole question, answer the detail asked, and add one polite expression.
أُرِيدُ is direct but polite when accompanied by مِنْ فَضْلِكَ / مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. أَعْطِنِي “give me” can sound too abrupt for this beginner restaurant context.

sorter.title: Build the transaction
sorter.instructions: Sort each line by its place in the restaurant exchange.

items.label: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. هَلْ هٰذِهِ الطَّاوِلَةُ شَاغِرَةٌ؟

listening.title: At Café Miftah
listening.script: النَّادِلُ: مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ. مَاذَا تُرِيدِينَ؟ الزَّبُونَةُ: أُرِيدُ سَلَطَةً وَسَانْدَوِيتْشَ جُبْنٍ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. النَّادِلُ: هَلْ تُرِيدِينَ شَيْئًا لِلشُّرْبِ؟ الزَّبُونَةُ: نَعَمْ، عَصِيرَ بُرْتُقَالٍ. النَّادِلُ: عَصِيرٌ صَغِيرٌ أَمْ كَبِيرٌ؟ الزَّبُونَةُ: صَغِيرٌ، شُكْرًا.

questions.prompt: What clarification does the waiter ask?

reading.title: Menu notice
reading.text: مَرْحَبًا بِكُمْ فِي مَقْهَى الزَّهْرَاءِ. نُقَدِّمُ الفُطُورَ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ إِلَى الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ. عِنْدَنَا خُبْزٌ وَجُبْنٌ وَبَيْضٌ، وَنُقَدِّمُ أَيْضًا حَسَاءَ العَدَسِ وَسَلَطَةً نَبَاتِيَّةً. لَا يُوجَدُ سَمَكٌ اليَوْمَ. المَشْرُوبَاتُ: شَايٌ، قَهْوَةٌ، حَلِيبٌ، مَاءٌ وَعَصِيرٌ. اُطْلُبُوا عِنْدَ الطَّاوِلَةِ، وَادْفَعُوا عِنْدَ البَابِ.

questions.feedback: مِنَ السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ إِلَى الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ.

prompts: Greet the waiter and ask for a menu.
Order one starter and one main dish.
Ask whether a vegetarian option is available.
Choose a drink and answer a size/type question.
Ask for the bill and close politely.
model: Good evening. What would you like?
أُرِيدُ حَسَاءَ العَدَسِ وَسَلَطَةً، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
I would like lentil soup and a salad, please.
Would you like something to drink?
نَعَمْ، مَاءً عَادِيًّا، ثُمَّ الحِسَابَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
Yes, still water, then the bill please.

writing.prompt: Write an 8-line café dialogue between a waiter and a customer. The customer must order food, choose a drink, answer one clarification and ask for the bill.
checklist: Use a greeting and a polite closing.
Include أُرِيدُ or هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَطْلُبَ.
Include at least one question from the waiter.
Use مِنْ فَضْلِكَ / مِنْ فَضْلِكِ accurately.
writing.model:
النَّادِلُ: مَرْحَبًا. مَاذَا تُرِيدُ؟
الزَّبُونُ: أُرِيدُ حَسَاءً وَسَانْدَوِيتْشًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
النَّادِلُ: هَلْ تُرِيدُ شَيْئًا لِلشُّرْبِ؟
الزَّبُونُ: نَعَمْ، عَصِيرَ تُفَّاحٍ.
النَّادِلُ: صَغِيرًا أَمْ كَبِيرًا؟
الزَّبُونُ: صَغِيرًا، شُكْرًا.
النَّادِلُ: شَيْءٌ آخَرُ؟
الزَّبُونُ: لَا، الحِسَابُ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

mistakes.why: The corrected form is more suitable for a polite restaurant exchange.
The requested item is the direct object and should be accusative.
عِنْدَكُمْ is a conventional way to ask a business whether it has something.

differentiation.core: Use a menu and sentence cards to complete a four-turn exchange.
differentiation.develop: Perform a six-turn role play with one unexpected clarification question.
differentiation.stretch: Handle an unavailable item, request an alternative and query the bill without returning to the model.

final.prompt: Which phrase is the most appropriate polite order?
final.feedback: It combines a request with politeness.
هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ asks whether the restaurant has it.

final.prompt: Which asks what a female wants?

grammar.title: Polite ordering with أُرِيدُ and price questions
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is a complete transactional frame: make a polite request, distinguish the form addressed to a man or woman, and ask the price accurately.

rules.heading: Order an item politely
rules.formula: أُرِيدُ + شَيْئًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ / مِنْ فَضْلِكِ
rules.explanation: The requested item follows أُرِيدُ. Use مِنْ فَضْلِكَ to a man and مِنْ فَضْلِكِ to a woman.

rules.heading: Ask whether something is available
rules.explanation: This polite business form asks whether the café or restaurant has an item.

rules.heading: Ask the price
rules.explanation: Use an idāfa phrase: “the price of the item”.

rules.heading: Close the exchange
rules.explanation: A complete transaction includes a polite closing.

grammar.common_error: Do not use a bare command such as أَعْطِنِي when practising a polite restaurant exchange. Use أُرِيدُ... مِنْ فَضْلِكَ/كِ.

quiz.feedback: The request is complete and includes politeness.

quiz.prompt: Ask whether vegetarian food is available.
quiz.feedback: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ asks about availability.

quiz.prompt: Which form of “please” addresses a female?
quiz.feedback: The final kasrah marks the female addressee form.

quiz.prompt: What does أَمْ do in a question?
quiz.feedback: أَمْ means “or” between alternatives.

quiz.prompt: Choose the polite request for the bill.
quiz.feedback: This is the conventional polite request.

quiz.prompt: Ask a girl “What would you like?”
quiz.feedback: The female listener form ends in ـِينَ.

quiz.prompt: Which is the polite request to a woman?
quiz.feedback: Use مِنْ فَضْلِكِ for a female addressee.
Use كَمْ سِعْرُ + the item in an idāfa phrase.

builders.target: I would like lentil soup and a salad, please.
Do you have vegetarian food?
The bill, please.

lessons.title: Menus, Prices and Dishes
lessons.summary: Read menus, calculate simple totals, ask and answer about prices, and explore several dishes from different Arabic-speaking communities without treating one cuisine as universal.
objectives: Read a structured Arabic menu and identify sections.
Ask and answer about prices using كَمْ ثَمَنُ ...؟
Calculate a simple food order using Arabic-Indic or Western numerals.
Recognise a selection of regional dishes and their main ingredients.
success: I can find an item and its price on a menu.
I can ask and answer كَمْ ثَمَنُ ...؟
I can total a small order.
I can describe one dish respectfully using يَتَكَوَّنُ مِنْ.

patterns.ar: كَمْ ثَمَنُ حَسَاءِ العَدَسِ؟ ثَمَنُهُ خَمْسَةُ دَنَانِيرَ.
patterns.en: How much is the lentil soup? It costs five dinars.
patterns.tip: Use كَمْ ثَمَنُ + item.

patterns.ar: الكَبْسَةُ طَبَقٌ تَقْلِيدِيٌّ يَتَكَوَّنُ مِنَ الأَرُزِّ وَاللَّحْمِ أَوِ الدَّجَاجِ.
patterns.en: Kabsa is a traditional dish consisting of rice and meat or chicken.
patterns.tip: A grammatically masculine predicate can describe the dish; the verb may follow the actual noun in fuller usage.

patterns.en: Maqluba consists of rice and vegetables.
patterns.tip: Feminine dish name → تَتَكَوَّنُ.

patterns.ar: الحُمُّصُ رَخِيصٌ، وَلٰكِنَّ الطَّبَقَ الرَّئِيسِيَّ غَالٍ.
patterns.en: Hummus is cheap, but the main dish is expensive.
patterns.tip: Compare value with رَخِيصٌ / غَالٍ.

patterns.en: The soup contains lentils and vegetables.
patterns.tip: Use يَحْتَوِي عَلَى to identify ingredients.

teach: Arabic-speaking communities have diverse cuisines shaped by geography, history, migration, family traditions and local ingredients. A dish may have several names or versions; present examples as specific rather than universal.
When calculating prices, the language objective is to locate and communicate information accurately. Use a calculator only after identifying the correct items and prices.

sorter.title: Which menu section?
sorter.instructions: Sort each item into the most likely menu section.

listening.title: A family order
listening.script: طَلَبَتِ الأُسْرَةُ حُمُّصًا بِأَرْبَعَةِ دَنَانِيرَ، وَسَلَطَةً بِخَمْسَةِ دَنَانِيرَ. طَلَبَ الأَبُ كَبْسَةً بِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ دِينَارًا، وَطَلَبَتِ الأُمُّ مَقْلُوبَةً بِعَشَرَةِ دَنَانِيرَ. شَرِبَ الطِّفْلَانِ عَصِيرَيْنِ، ثَمَنُ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ ثَلَاثَةُ دَنَانِيرَ.

questions.prompt: How much is the mother’s dish?
What is the total for the two juices?

reading.title: Menu: Bayt al-Diyafa
reading.text:
قَائِمَةُ بَيْتِ الضِّيَافَةِ
المُقَبِّلَاتُ: حُمُّصٌ ٤، تَبُّولَةٌ ٥، فَلَافِلُ ٦.
الأَطْبَاقُ الرَّئِيسِيَّةُ: كُسْكُسٌ بِالخَضْرَوَاتِ ١٠، كَبْسَةُ الدَّجَاجِ ١٢، مَنْسَفٌ ١٤.
الحَلْوَيَاتُ: كَعْكٌ ٤، فَاكِهَةٌ طَازَجَةٌ ٥.
المَشْرُوبَاتُ: مَاءٌ ٢، شَايٌ ٣، عَصِيرٌ ٤.
مُلَاحَظَةٌ: الكُسْكُسُ بِالخَضْرَوَاتِ طَبَقٌ نَبَاتِيٌّ.
عَلَى كُلِّ طَاوِلَةٍ طَبَقٌ وَشَوْكَةٌ وَسِكِّينٌ وَمِلْعَقَةٌ وَمَنْدِيلٌ. يُقَدَّمُ الحَسَاءُ فِي وِعَاءٍ، وَيُقَدَّمُ الشَّايُ فِي كُوبٍ، وَالعَصِيرُ فِي كَأْسٍ.
مُلَاحَظَةٌ أُخْرَى: يَحْتَوِي الحُمُّصُ عَلَى الحُمُّصِ المَطْحُونِ وَالزَّيْتِ.

questions.feedback: The note identifies it as نَبَاتِيٌّ.

questions.prompt: How much are kabsa and water together?
What is the total for falafel, tea and cake?
Which utensil is used for soup?
questions.feedback: The table has a مِلْعَقَةٌ and soup is served in a bowl.

questions.prompt: How are tea and juice served?
options: tea in a cup and juice in a glass
tea in a bowl and juice in a jug
questions.feedback: الشَّايُ فِي كُوبٍ، وَالعَصِيرُ فِي كَأْسٍ.

model: And what does it consist of?
It consists of rice, chicken and spices.

writing.prompt: Design a concise Arabic menu with at least two starters, three main dishes, two desserts and three drinks. Add prices, then write four sentences describing value and ingredients.
checklist: Organise the menu under clear Arabic headings.
Use numerals consistently and add a currency word.
Use يَتَكَوَّنُ / تَتَكَوَّنُ مِنْ twice.
Include one comparison using أَرْخَصُ / أَغْلَى or رَخِيصٌ / غَالٍ.
writing.model: المُقَبِّلَاتُ: حُمُّصٌ ٤، سَلَطَةٌ ٥. الأَطْبَاقُ الرَّئِيسِيَّةُ: كَبْسَةٌ ١٢، مَقْلُوبَةٌ ١٠، كُسْكُسٌ ١١. المَشْرُوبَاتُ: مَاءٌ ٢، شَايٌ ٣، عَصِيرٌ ٤. الكَبْسَةُ تَتَكَوَّنُ مِنَ الأَرُزِّ وَالدَّجَاجِ. السَّلَطَةُ تَتَكَوَّنُ مِنْ خَضْرَوَاتٍ طَازَجَةٍ. المَاءُ أَرْخَصُ مِنَ العَصِيرِ.

mistakes.right: كَمْ ثَمَنُ الحَسَاءِ؟ / كَمْ سِعْرُ الحَسَاءِ؟
mistakes.why: Use a complete idafa question: price of the soup.
The feminine dish name takes تَتَكَوَّنُ.
Use the appropriate plural after five.

differentiation.core: Read a menu and answer price questions with a number and item.
differentiation.develop: Calculate three order totals and describe one dish’s ingredients.
differentiation.stretch: Compare two menus for price, variety and dietary options in a short recommendation.

final.feedback: كَمْ ثَمَنُهُ؟ means how much is it?

options: All Arab food is the same.
Dishes vary across regions and families.
Only one country has traditional food.
final.feedback: The unit presents diversity and variation accurately.

grammar.title: Asking and answering prices with كَمْ
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is the price question كَمْ and accurate number–currency phrases. Menu descriptions also recycle agreement and the high-value structures يَتَكَوَّنُ مِنْ and يُقَدَّمُ مَعَ.

rules.heading: Ask the price
rules.explanation: Use كَمْ followed by “price/cost of” and the menu item.

rules.heading: State a price
rules.explanation: Use ـهُ for a masculine item and ـهَا for a feminine item.

rules.heading: Describe ingredients
rules.explanation: The verb agrees with the dish name.

rules.heading: Say what accompanies a dish
rules.explanation: Use the masculine or feminine passive form according to the dish.

grammar.common_error: Do not write كَمْ السِّعْرُ الحَسَاءُ؟ Use the complete phrase كَمْ سِعْرُ الحَسَاءِ؟

quiz.feedback: كَمْ ثَمَنُ asks for the price.
المَقْلُوبَةُ is feminine.
Use feminine تَحْتَوِي with السَّلَطَةُ.

quiz.prompt: Which means “its price” for a feminine dish?
quiz.feedback: ـهَا refers back to a feminine noun.

quiz.prompt: Choose the matching adjective for الكَبْسَةُ.
quiz.feedback: The adjective agrees with the feminine dish name.
The fixed phrase is يَحْتَوِي عَلَى.
The feminine dish name takes تَتَكَوَّنُ.
After five, use the plural دَنَانِيرَ.

builders.target: How much is the lentil soup? It costs five dinars.
Maqluba consists of rice and vegetables.
The soup contains lentils.

lessons.title: The Body and Its Parts
lessons.summary: Name and locate a comprehensive set of body parts, use demonstratives and possessive forms, and understand simple descriptions of what body parts do.
objectives: Recognise and name major external body parts.
Use هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ and possessive suffixes with body nouns.
Recognise common dual forms for paired body parts.
Understand simple statements about seeing, hearing, smelling, touching and movement.
success: I can label at least fifteen body parts.
I can choose هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ accurately.
I can say “my head”, “my hand” and “my eyes”.
I can understand a short body description.

patterns.en: This is my head, and this is my hand.
patterns.tip: Choose the demonstrative according to noun gender.

patterns.en: I have two eyes and two ears.
patterns.tip: The dual ending -انِ signals two in this form.

patterns.en: We see with our eyes and hear with our ears.
patterns.tip: بِـ can express the body part used.

patterns.ar: القَلْبُ فِي الصَّدْرِ، وَالمَعِدَةُ فِي البَطْنِ.
patterns.en: The heart is in the chest, and the stomach is in the abdomen.
patterns.tip: Use فِي to locate internal organs.

teach: Some body nouns do not have the gender students may expect. Learn the word together with a demonstrative or adjective: هٰذِهِ يَدٌ، هٰذِهِ عَيْنٌ، هٰذَا رَأْسٌ.
Dual forms are introduced for recognition and useful paired nouns. The core goal is communication, not a complete dual-case paradigm.

sorter.title: Masculine or feminine?
sorter.instructions: Sort the body noun by the demonstrative it takes.

listening.title: Listen and identify the body part
listening.script: أَرَى بِعَيْنَيَّ، وَأَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنَيَّ. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي، وَآكُلُ بِفَمِي. أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي اليُمْنَى، وَأَرْكُضُ بِرِجْلَيَّ وَقَدَمَيَّ. عِنْدَمَا أَتَعَبُ، أَضَعُ يَدِي عَلَى صَدْرِي وَأَتَنَفَّسُ بِعُمْقٍ.

questions.prompt: Which body part is used to see?
Which body part is used to smell?
Which hand is used for writing?
What does the speaker do when tired?
options: puts a hand on the chest and breathes deeply
questions.feedback: The final sentence states both actions.

reading.title: A body science note
reading.text: الجِسْمُ نِظَامٌ مُتَكَامِلٌ. فِي الرَّأْسِ عَيْنَانِ لِلرُّؤْيَةِ وَأُذُنَانِ لِلسَّمْعِ، وَفِي الوَجْهِ أَنْفٌ لِلشَّمِّ وَفَمٌ لِلْأَكْلِ وَالكَلَامِ. القَلْبُ فِي الصَّدْرِ وَيَعْمَلُ دَائِمًا. العِظَامُ تَدْعَمُ الجِسْمَ، وَالجِلْدُ يَحْمِيهِ. نَسْتَخْدِمُ أَيْدِيَنَا لِلْكِتَابَةِ وَاللَّمْسِ، وَأَقْدَامَنَا لِلْمَشْيِ.

questions.prompt: How many eyes and ears are mentioned?
What is the mouth used for?

writing.prompt: Write 7–8 sentences describing the body and what selected parts do. Include four possessive forms, two dual forms and two action verbs.
checklist: Use هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ accurately.
Include عَيْنَانِ، أُذُنَانِ، يَدَانِ or قَدَمَانِ.
Use at least two of يَرَى، يَسْمَعُ، يَشُمُّ، يَلْمِسُ، يَتَنَفَّسُ.
Check feminine nouns such as يَدٌ، عَيْنٌ، قَدَمٌ.
writing.model: هٰذَا رَأْسِي، وَهٰذَا وَجْهِي. لِي عَيْنَانِ وَأُذُنَانِ. أَرَى بِعَيْنَيَّ وَأَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنَيَّ. هٰذِهِ يَدِي اليُمْنَى، وَهٰذِهِ يَدِي اليُسْرَى. أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي، وَأَمْشِي بِقَدَمَيَّ. القَلْبُ فِي صَدْرِي.

mistakes.why: يَدٌ is grammatically feminine.
Use the dual noun form for two eyes.
Hearing is associated with the ear; the correction also reinforces the correct noun.

differentiation.core: Label twelve body parts with a word bank and select the correct demonstrative.
differentiation.develop: Explain the function of six body parts in complete sentences.
differentiation.stretch: Produce a short science-style explanation using duals, plurals and purpose phrases لِـ.

final.prompt: Which body part is used for smelling?
final.feedback: The nose is used for smelling.

final.prompt: Where is the heart located in the model?
final.feedback: The heart is in the chest.

grammar.title: هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ and the dual
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is choosing the correct demonstrative for the grammatical gender of a body part and using the dual form for paired body parts.

rules.heading: Use هٰذَا with masculine nouns
rules.explanation: Use هٰذَا with masculine body-part nouns.

rules.heading: Use هٰذِهِ with feminine nouns
rules.explanation: Some body-part nouns are grammatically feminine even without ـة.

rules.heading: Form the dual
rules.explanation: Paired body parts often use the dual rather than the number اثنان.

rules.heading: Add the possessive ending
rules.explanation: The ending ـي means “my”.

grammar.common_error: Do not choose هٰذَا only by looking for ـة. يَدٌ، عَيْنٌ and أُذُنٌ are feminine: هٰذِهِ يَدِي.

quiz.feedback: يَدٌ is grammatically feminine.
The suffix ـي means “my”.
The ending ـانِ marks the dual here.
بِـ expresses the body part used.

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct demonstrative for أَنْفٌ.
quiz.feedback: أَنْفٌ is masculine singular.
Use فِي to say where it is.
يَدٌ is feminine.
Use the dual form عَيْنَانِ.

builders.target: This is my head and this is my hand.
I see with my eyes and hear with my ears.
The heart is in the chest.

lessons.title: Health Problems and How You Feel
lessons.summary: Describe common symptoms, locate pain, say how long a problem has lasted and understand simple questions about health.
objectives: Name common illnesses, injuries and symptoms.
Use عِنْدِي and أَشْعُرُ بِـ to describe a health problem.
Locate pain using عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي ...
Use مُنْذُ with a simple duration phrase.
success: I can say how I feel.
I can name at least ten common health problems.
I can identify where something hurts.
I can understand and answer مُنْذُ مَتَى؟

patterns.en: I have a headache and a fever.
patterns.tip: Use عِنْدِي + symptom.

patterns.en: I feel pain in my stomach.
patterns.tip: أَشْعُرُ بِـ introduces a feeling or pain.

patterns.en: My teeth have hurt for two days.
patterns.tip: The body part can be the subject of the pain expression.

patterns.ar: أَنَا مُصَابٌ بِالزُّكَامِ. / أَنَا مُصَابَةٌ بِالزُّكَامِ.
patterns.en: I have a cold. (m/f)
patterns.tip: Make مُصَابٌ / مُصَابَةٌ agree with the speaker.

teach: Choose one clear structure and complete it accurately. عِنْدِي صُدَاعٌ is a simple possession pattern; أَشْعُرُ بِصُدَاعٍ uses a preposition; يُؤْلِمُنِي رَأْسِي makes the body part the thing that hurts.
Health descriptions should remain factual and age-appropriate. The lesson teaches language, not diagnosis. Serious or persistent symptoms require an appropriate adult or healthcare professional.

sorter.title: Symptom, injury or feeling?
sorter.instructions: Sort each phrase by what it describes.

listening.title: Four callers to a clinic
listening.script: المُتَّصِلُ الأَوَّلُ عِنْدَهُ صُدَاعٌ وَحُمَّى مُنْذُ أَمْسِ. المُتَّصِلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ تُؤْلِمُهَا أَسْنَانُهَا مُنْذُ أُسْبُوعٍ. المُتَّصِلُ الثَّالِثُ سَقَطَ، وَعِنْدَهُ جُرْحٌ فِي رُكْبَتِهِ. المُتَّصِلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ أَكَلَتْ طَعَامًا وَأَصْبَحَ عِنْدَهَا أَلَمٌ فِي المَعِدَةِ وَغَثَيَانٌ. المُتَّصِلُ الخَامِسُ سَقَطَ مِنَ الدَّرَجِ وَكَسَرَ ذِرَاعَهُ. وَالمُتَّصِلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ تَشْعُرُ بِالمَرَضِ وَتَتَقَيَّأُ.

questions.prompt: How long has caller 2 had tooth pain?
Which two problems does caller 4 have?
What happened to the fifth caller?
options: He fell and broke his arm.

questions.prompt: What is the sixth caller doing?

reading.title: Health messages
reading.text:
الرِّسَالَةُ ١: لَنْ آتِيَ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ اليَوْمَ؛ عِنْدِي زُكَامٌ وَسُعَالٌ، وَأَشْعُرُ بِالتَّعَبِ.
الرِّسَالَةُ ٢: سَقَطْتُ فِي المَلْعَبِ، وَعِنْدِي إِصَابَةٌ فِي كَاحِلِي. لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ المَشْيَ جَيِّدًا.
الرِّسَالَةُ ٣: عِنْدِي حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ بَعْضِ الأَطْعِمَةِ، لِذٰلِكَ أَقْرَأُ المُكَوِّنَاتِ قَبْلَ الأَكْلِ.
الرِّسَالَةُ ٤: جَرَحَ أَخِي إِصْبَعَهُ فِي المَطْبَخِ، فَغَسَلَ الجُرْحَ وَوَضَعَ عَلَيْهِ ضِمَادًا نَظِيفًا.

questions.prompt: What does writer 3 do before eating?
What did the brother do after cutting his finger?
options: washed the wound and used a clean bandage
questions.feedback: He washed the wound and used ضِمَادًا نَظِيفًا.

model: I have a headache and feel tired.

writing.prompt: Write four short patient messages. Each message should name a different problem, body location where relevant, and duration or cause.
checklist: Use at least two different structures: عِنْدِي / أَشْعُرُ بِـ / يُؤْلِمُنِي.
Include two body parts.
Use مُنْذُ correctly at least once.
Make مَرِيضٌ / مُصَابٌ agree with the speaker where used.
writing.model: ١. عِنْدِي صُدَاعٌ وَحُمَّى مُنْذُ أَمْسِ. ٢. أَشْعُرُ بِأَلَمٍ فِي المَعِدَةِ. ٣. سَقَطْتُ وَعِنْدِي جُرْحٌ فِي رُكْبَتِي. ٤. أَنَا مُصَابَةٌ بِالزُّكَامِ وَأَشْعُرُ بِالتَّعَبِ.

mistakes.why: Use فِي to locate pain in a body part.
أَشْعُرُ requires بِـ; عِنْدِي can take the symptom directly.
The adjective/participle agrees with the speaker.

differentiation.core: Match ten symptoms to pictures and complete عِنْدِي sentence frames.
differentiation.develop: Describe four health problems with location and duration, then answer follow-up questions.
differentiation.stretch: Write a short clinic triage note distinguishing symptom, duration, cause and impact.

final.feedback: مُنْذُ مَتَى؟ asks since when/how long.

grammar.title: عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي... and simple illness sentences
grammar.arabic: عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي... وَجُمَلُ المَرَضِ البَسِيطَةُ
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is the fixed health frame عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي plus a body part, followed by simple sentences that name an illness and agree with the speaker.

rules.heading: Locate pain
rules.explanation: Use the complete chunk عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي and then name the affected body part, often with a possessive ending.

rules.heading: Name an illness directly
rules.explanation: Common illnesses and symptoms can follow عِنْدِي directly.

rules.heading: Agree with the speaker
rules.explanation: The adjective changes according to whether the speaker is male or female.

rules.heading: Add duration
rules.explanation: Use مُنْذُ to say how long the problem has continued.

grammar.common_error: Use فِي to locate pain: عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي المَعِدَةِ, not عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ عَلَى المَعِدَةِ.

quiz.feedback: عِنْدِي + symptom is the simplest pattern.
The fixed structure is أَشْعُرُ بِـ.
The phrase names the teeth as the source of pain.
مُنْذُ introduces duration from a starting point.
مُصَابَةٌ agrees with a female speaker.
أَشْعُرُ requires بِـ before the feeling/symptom.

quiz.prompt: Choose “I have pain in my back.”
quiz.feedback: The fixed frame uses فِي.

quiz.prompt: Choose the form for a female speaker.
quiz.feedback: مَرِيضَةٌ agrees with a female speaker.

builders.target: I have a headache and fever since yesterday.
I feel pain in my stomach.
My teeth have hurt for a week.

lessons.title: At the Doctor and Pharmacy
lessons.summary: Take part in a simple consultation, understand safe general advice, request medicine or an appointment, and distinguish doctor, dentist, nurse, hospital and pharmacy contexts.
objectives: Use key people, places and objects in healthcare settings.
Describe symptoms clearly to a doctor or pharmacist.
Understand and give simple advice with يَجِبُ أَنْ and imperatives.
Perform a structured doctor/pharmacy role play.
success: I can explain a simple health problem.
I can understand three pieces of general advice.
I can ask for medicine or an appointment politely.
I can complete a consultation dialogue.

patterns.en: I have a fever and cough for two days.
patterns.tip: Give symptom + duration clearly.

patterns.ar: يَجِبُ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحَ وَأَنْ تَشْرَبَ المَاءَ.
patterns.en: You should rest and drink water.
patterns.tip: After أَنْ, use the appropriate subjunctive form; at Foundation, learn the whole advice chunk.

patterns.en: I would like medicine for a headache, please.
patterns.tip: Use لِـ to state what the medicine is for.

patterns.ar: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ مَوْعِدًا مَعَ طَبِيبِ الأَسْنَانِ.
patterns.en: I would like to book an appointment with the dentist.
patterns.tip: This is a useful complete appointment phrase.

teach: The doctor or pharmacist needs specific information: symptom, location, duration and any relevant cause. Give one detail at a time and respond to follow-up questions.
Advice in this lesson is language practice and deliberately general. It does not replace professional medical assessment.

sorter.title: Where should the person go?
sorter.instructions: Sort each need by the most suitable first destination.

listening.title: Doctor–patient consultation
listening.script: الطَّبِيبَةُ: مَا المُشْكِلَةُ؟ المَرِيضُ: عِنْدِي حُمَّى وَسُعَالٌ مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ، وَأَشْعُرُ بِأَلَمٍ فِي الحَلْقِ. الطَّبِيبَةُ: سَأَفْحَصُ دَرَجَةَ حَرَارَتِكَ. اِفْتَحْ فَمَكَ وَتَنَفَّسْ بِعُمْقٍ. يَجِبُ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحَ وَأَنْ تَشْرَبَ مَاءً كَثِيرًا. خُذْ هٰذَا الدَّوَاءَ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي اليَوْمِ.

questions.prompt: How long has the patient been ill?
What two lifestyle instructions are given?
How often should the medicine be taken?

reading.title: Pharmacy instructions
reading.text: مَرْحَبًا. هٰذَا الدَّوَاءُ لِلزُّكَامِ وَالسُّعَالِ. خُذْ حَبَّةً وَاحِدَةً بَعْدَ الفُطُورِ وَحَبَّةً أُخْرَى بَعْدَ العَشَاءِ. لَا تَأْخُذِ الدَّوَاءَ عَلَى مَعِدَةٍ فَارِغَةٍ. اِشْرَبْ مَاءً كَثِيرًا، وَإِذَا لَمْ تَتَحَسَّنْ فَتَحَدَّثْ مَعَ الطَّبِيبِ. اِقْرَأِ التَّعْلِيمَاتِ عَلَى العُلْبَةِ.

questions.prompt: When is the first tablet taken?
How many tablets per day are described?
questions.feedback: One after breakfast and one after dinner.

options: taking it on an empty stomach
questions.feedback: لَا تَأْخُذِ الدَّوَاءَ عَلَى مَعِدَةٍ فَارِغَةٍ.

questions.prompt: What should the person do if not improving?

prompts: Answer where the pain is or how you feel.
Ask how often to take the medicine.
model: I have a headache and fever since yesterday.
يَجِبُ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحِي وَأَنْ تَشْرَبِي المَاءَ.
You should rest and drink water.
Thank you. How many times do I take the medicine?

writing.prompt: Write a complete 10-line consultation between a healthcare professional and patient. Include symptoms, duration, one examination instruction, two pieces of advice and medicine frequency.
checklist: Use professional roles and greetings accurately.
Use عِنْدِي / أَشْعُرُ بِـ for symptoms.
Use يَجِبُ أَنْ or an imperative for advice.
Include كَمْ مَرَّةً؟ or مَتَى آخُذُ الدَّوَاءَ؟
writing.model:
الطَّبِيبُ: مَا المُشْكِلَةُ؟
المَرِيضُ: عِنْدِي سُعَالٌ وَأَلَمٌ فِي الحَلْقِ مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ.
الطَّبِيبُ: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حُمَّى؟
المَرِيضُ: نَعَمْ، وَأَشْعُرُ بِالتَّعَبِ.
الطَّبِيبُ: اِفْتَحْ فَمَكَ وَتَنَفَّسْ بِعُمْقٍ.
المَرِيضُ: حَسَنًا.
الطَّبِيبُ: يَجِبُ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحَ وَأَنْ تَشْرَبَ المَاءَ. خُذْ هٰذَا الدَّوَاءَ.
المَرِيضُ: كَمْ مَرَّةً آخُذُهُ؟
الطَّبِيبُ: مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي اليَوْمِ.
المَرِيضُ: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.

mistakes.why: The model uses the subjunctive ending after أَنْ.
The requested medicine is a direct object.
After the verb in this phrase, use the accusative dual form مَرَّتَيْنِ.

differentiation.core: Complete a doctor dialogue from a phrase bank and identify three instructions.
differentiation.develop: Perform a role play with symptom, duration, examination and advice.
differentiation.stretch: Switch between doctor and pharmacy contexts and handle an unplanned follow-up question.

final.feedback: After أَنْ in this model, use تَشْرَبَ.

final.prompt: Which imperative means rest (to a female)?
final.feedback: اِسْتَرِيحِي is addressed to a female.

final.prompt: How do you ask how often?
final.feedback: كَمْ مَرَّةً؟ asks how many times.

options: The language supports communication; professionals diagnose.
All symptoms need the same medicine.
final.feedback: The lesson explicitly separates language practice from diagnosis.

grammar.title: Advice with يَجِبُ أَنْ
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is the advice frame يَجِبُ أَنْ followed by a verb. The verb form after أَنْ is learned and practised as a complete useful chunk.

rules.heading: Give essential advice
rules.explanation: Use this frame for an important medical or health recommendation.

rules.heading: Join two actions
rules.explanation: Repeat أَنْ before the second verb when joining two pieces of advice.
examples: يَجِبُ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحَ وَأَنْ تَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا.

rules.heading: Request medicine
rules.explanation: The medicine is a direct object; لِـ introduces the symptom or purpose.

rules.heading: Give dosage frequency
rules.explanation: Use the accusative dual مَرَّتَيْنِ in this time expression.

grammar.title: يَجِبُ / مِنَ الأَفْضَلِ أَنْ for healthy habits
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus compares strong and gentler advice frames, then connects the advice to a reason.

rules.heading: Give strong advice
rules.explanation: Use يَجِبُ أَنْ for an important recommendation.

rules.heading: Give gentler advice
rules.explanation: This frame means “it is better to” and softens the recommendation.
examples: مِنَ الأَفْضَلِ أَنْ نَمْشِيَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

rules.heading: Give negative advice
rules.explanation: Use the negative frame to discourage an unhealthy action.
examples: لَا يَجِبُ أَنْ نُكْثِرَ مِنَ الحَلْوَيَاتِ.

rules.heading: Explain the advice
rules.explanation: لِأَنَّ introduces the reason; لِذٰلِكَ introduces the result or recommendation.

rows: لَا يَجِبُ أَنْ تُكْثِرَ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ.

grammar.common_error: A verb must follow أَنْ: يَجِبُ أَنْ نَشْرَبَ, not يَجِبُ أَنْ المَاءُ.

مِنَ الأَفْضَلِ أَنْ softens the advice.

patterns.ar: لِلْحِفَاظِ عَلَى صِحَّتِي، يَجِبُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَ المَاءَ وَأَنْ أُمَارِسَ الرِّيَاضَةَ.

patterns.ar: أَخِيرًا، هَدَفِي أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا وَأَنْ أُقَلِّلَ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ.

patterns.tip: End with a specific next step.

teach: A developed answer normally contains at least two pieces of information: an answer plus a reason, example, comparison or time detail. Aim for meaningful extension rather than speaking quickly.
In writing, content comes first, then organisation, then accuracy. Plan the ideas, write a complete draft, and only then use the check routine: verbs → gender → reasons → connectives → spelling.

grammar.title: Connectives for a food-and-health paragraph
grammar.arabic: أَدَوَاتُ الرَّبْطِ فِي فِقْرَةٍ عَنِ الطَّعَامِ وَالصِّحَّةِ
grammar.overview: The lesson-plan grammar focus is organising a 6–8 sentence paragraph with sequence, addition and contrast. The connectives must show a real relationship between ideas.

rules.heading: Sequence actions
rules.explanation: Use sequence words to organise meals, habits or a daily routine.

rules.heading: Add another detail
rules.explanation: Use addition connectives when the next idea supports or extends the first.

rules.heading: Show contrast
rules.explanation: Use وَلٰكِنْ when the second idea differs from the first.
examples: أُحِبُّ الحَلْوَيَاتِ، وَلٰكِنْ لَا آكُلُهَا كَثِيرًا.

rules.heading: Develop an opinion
rules.explanation: A developed paragraph gives a precise opinion and explains why.
examples: أُفَضِّلُ الطَّعَامَ المَنْزِلِيَّ لِأَنَّهُ طَازَجٌ وَصِحِّيٌّ.

grammar.common_error: Do not add connectives only to increase a count. Choose the connective that matches the relationship between the ideas.
